correctness.rationale: For 1<b<=2, the modulation Poisson identity gives only the 0,+1,-1 Walnut shifts because q=1/b>=1/2. Since q=2a, the coefficients are G0=2+M and G_{+-1}=-M, with the exact a-periodic counting function M taking the essential values {0,1}, {1}, {1,2}, or {2} in the four parameter regions. Fiber Fourier diagonalization gives multiplier [2+M-2M cos(theta)]/b and thus the exact essential range, spectrum, spectral gap and eigenvalue classification. For b>3/2 the multiplier has a zero only on an angular null set, proving injective nonframe behavior. A fresh exact-Fraction checker confirmed 34228 finite coefficient/spectral consistency assertions; the infinite-range proof is analytic, not enumerative.

value.rationale: The fixed redundancy-two Haar frame set is an independently motivated natural operator family. The first nonpainless overlap region permits a complete nonconstant spectral and spectral-type classification; the sharp gap stays positive at the qualitative frame endpoint but immediately becomes zero beyond it, yet the system remains complete. A persistently embedded eigenvalue disappears at the exact endpoint. This sharp operator-level transition, not a small numerical tweak, measures stability versus completeness for a discontinuous signed analysis window.
